title: Prefill: MegaMoE FI NVFP4 (2x8K) + shared-expert side stream
shape: DEP16 F16K (3 x 5,456 tok) at L78K, NVFP4; MegaMoE T=16384 tokens/rank, 56 experts/GPU, 92 layers; shared MXFP8 gate_up [12288,7168] + down [7168,6144]
basis: PROJECTED (reviewed ledger); first standalone EP4-emulation measurements queued (r1/r2)
gap_analysis: Model (optables nvfp4_modelopt|P3-16|prefill): MegaMoE layer = max(ops 1.05, link 1.97) + exposed = 2.151 ms/layer (197.9 ms/step); shared MXFP8 37.4 ms/step. The NVFP4 EP16 MegaMoE is NVLink-bound on the BF16 combine (FI SOL ledger: 8K call = 1256 us of which combine ~823 us at the measured link rate; MMA ~258 us), so the tensor cores idle ~75% of the layer. Current in-step path (code reading): one 16K-capacity launch with the i8192 S2/N256 record knobs, 4 kernels per call (stage, router, persistent main, top-k reduce), shared experts serial after MegaMoE in the TP1 DEP path (the SP side-stream overlap is not taken at TP1). Vendored vs FI kernel at 8K differs by ~2% in tuner numbers (1282 vs 1254 us), so the ledger's 281-358 ms in-step range is unverified; r1 measures vendored 8K/16K vs FI 8K/16K at the per-rank shape, r2 the 2x8K sub-calls with the shared expert overlapped at persistent-grid caps.
inefficiencies: Shared experts serial after MegaMoE on the TP1 DEP path (~40-64 ms/step exposed; model hides them under the link-bound MegaMoE) [code + release-tree profile]
Single 16K-capacity MegaMoE call vs 2x8K sub-calls (FI: 2649 vs 2x1254 us) [FI measured; vendored to measure]
Router kernel 0.34 ms/layer exclusive in the release-tree F8K profile (sizes round + metadata push; includes rank skew) [measured MX, cause hypothesis]
BF16 combine at ~1.07 TB/s vs model link 1.146 TB/s; 2.5% of combine bytes avoidable only by an FP32 per-rank pre-reduction (not worth it) [analysis]
